newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canada's Chretien starts visit to France.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien starts visit to France.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien arrived in France on Tuesday for an official three-day visit expected to focus on trade and economic exchanges.
Chretien was met by junior Trade Minister Yves Galland and given military honours at Orly airport, south of Paris.
Chretien, who is accompanied by Industry Minister John Manley, will dine with French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Wednesday and lunch with President Jacques Chirac on Thursday.
Diplomats said they expected deals to be announced between French and Canadian high-technology companies, including the space, computer and broadcasting industries.
Paris and Ottawa belong to the G7 group of industrialised countries, and Canada is an associate partner of the European Space Agency ESA.

On a visit to Canada last June, Juppe said France would stand by the mainly French-speaking province of Quebec whatever political future it chose. The risk of the province separating from Canada, with the possible encouragement of France, is a constant concern for Ottawa.
Anxious to push bilateral trade, Juppe repeatedly mentioned the idea of using French technology to build a high-speed railway linking Ontario and Quebec.
But Canadian Industry Minister John Manley has said it would require enormous public spending at a time when Canada is fighting high deficits.
